company: HomeCo Daily Needs REIT (managed by HMC Funds Management Limited, a member of the HMC Capital Group)
title: HMC Capital Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: A person who is an employee, officer or director of a Group Entity, and includes Senior Executives.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of a Group Entity; distinguished for the pre-approval routing (Chair and Group Company Secretary, in consultation with the Group CEO), the 2-business-day post-trade notification, and the margin lending consent regime.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: The CEO and CFO of a Group Entity, all direct reports to the CEO, other AASB 124 key management personnel, and any other Employee the Board designates as a Senior Executive; distinguished for the 2-business-day post-trade notification and the margin lending consent regime.

tiers.name: Designated Staff Members
tiers.description: Employees with access to sensitive information about the Group's trading or intended trading positions in Third Party Securities (e.g. research staff, those aware of Group positions or M&A activity, those making trading recommendations, or fund management staff); subject to a Restricted List pre-clearance regime for Third Party Securities, separate from HMC Capital Group Securities.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse, children and other family members, and any trusts, companies, nominees and other persons over whom the Director or Employee has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into transactions or arrangements, including by way of derivatives or similar financial products, which operate to limit the economic risk relating to HMC Capital Group Securities granted under an employee, executive or director incentive plan or as part of the Employee's remuneration

windows.end_anchor: 1 business day after release of the half year accounts to the ASX
1 business day after release of the annual accounts to the ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Group Board (including in consultation with the Board of a Group Entity) may declare a Blackout Period at any time, at its absolute discretion, without prior notice, and for any one or more HMC Capital Group Securities, e.g. where Directors believe certain Employees may hold inside information. Additional restrictions may also be placed on Trading (e.g. a significant transaction with an external listed entity), notified by the Group Company Secretary. Confidentiality of these additional restrictions is not addressed, though notification of Blackout Period commencement/cessation is sent by email to all Directors and Employees.

rules.detail: Financial Products are expressly defined to include swaps, futures, CFDs, options, warrants and other derivatives over HMC Capital Group Securities, with no venue restriction. Pre-approval is required for every proposed Trade at any time, not only during a Blackout Period.
rules.evidence: Financial Products means any structured financial products, swaps, futures contracts, contracts for difference, spread bets, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of any HMC Capital Group Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no consent route, on derivatives or similar products limiting the economic risk of incentive-plan or remuneration securities that have not vested.
rules.evidence: entering into transactions or arrangements, including by way of derivatives or similar financial products, which operate to limit the economic risk relating to HMC Capital Group Securities granted under an employee, executive or director incentive plan or as part of the Employee's remuneration, which either have not vested or have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or other restriction on dealing under the terms of the plan

rules.detail: Same absolute ban extends to vested securities that remain subject to a holding lock or other dealing restriction under the plan.
rules.evidence: or have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or other restriction on dealing under the terms of the plan

rules.detail: Once vested and unrestricted, a hedge is treated as ordinary Trading requiring prior written pre-approval and compliance with Blackout Periods and insider trading law.
rules.evidence: When permitted to Trade in accordance with this Policy ... all Directors and Employees must give a prior written request for pre-approval to the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary of any proposed Trading in HMC Capital Group Securities

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure that limits economic risk of the securities falls within the hedging definition and is banned outright over unvested incentive/remuneration securities.
rules.evidence: entering into transactions or arrangements, including by way of derivatives or similar financial products, which operate to limit the economic risk relating to HMC Capital Group Securities

rules.detail: Over vested, unrestricted units, a monetisation is at minimum an agreement to sell, a Trade requiring the same pre-approval as any other dealing.
rules.evidence: entering into an agreement to buy or sell HMC Capital Group Securities

rules.detail: Named as 'short positions': an outright ban on Trading that lets an Employee profit from, or limit the economic risk of, a decrease in the market price of HMC Capital Group Securities; catches short sales and economically equivalent derivative positions alike.
rules.evidence: (short positions) Trading in HMC Capital Group Securities which enable an Employee to profit from or limit the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of HMC Capital Group Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

'Contracts for difference' are expressly named in the Financial Products definition; a CFD is dealt with like any other derivative dealing (pre-approval required at any time), and a CFD structured to profit from or limit the risk of a price decrease is additionally caught by the short positions ban.
rules.evidence: swaps, futures contracts, contracts for difference, spread bets, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of any HMC Capital Group Securities

rules.detail: Consent of the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary (Chair of the Company for their own arrangements) is required before including the securities in a margin loan portfolio, transferring them into an existing margin loan account, or otherwise trading pursuant to a margin lending arrangement.
rules.evidence: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in HMC Capital Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary

rules.detail: Same consent requirement applies to Senior Executives as to Directors.
rules.evidence: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in HMC Capital Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary

rules.detail: Encumbrance is not named as a distinct concept; the operative restriction is 'transferring HMC Capital Group Securities into an existing margin loan account' (i.e. pledging them as collateral), which needs the same CEO/Company Secretary (or Chair) consent as entering the margin loan itself.
rules.evidence: transferring HMC Capital Group Securities into an existing margin loan account

rules.detail: Only margin lending arrangements are named as a form of secured financing; the consent requirement is the operative control, not a scope limited to broker margin loans given the 'or otherwise Trade ... pursuant to a margin lending arrangement' language.
rules.evidence: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in HMC Capital Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary (or, in the case of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary, the Chair of the Company).

rules.detail: Ban on buying and selling within six months and other short-term dealings such as forward contracts; carve-out for exercising employee options/performance rights and for the sale of securities converted following such exercise.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling HMC Capital Group Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (e.g. forward contracts). However, the sale of HMC Capital Group Securities that have been converted after exercising options or rights will not be regarded as short-term trading

clearance.approver: Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: Upon receipt of the Pre-approval Request, the Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Company Secretary must either approve or reject the Trade ... If the Pre-approval Request is approved, the opportunity to make the Trade expires five trading days from the date the approval is received.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Company and Group Company Secretary, in consultation with the Group Chief Executive Officer
clearance.evidence: unless the Pre-approval Request is received from a Director where, subject to clause 6.2, it must be approved by the Chair and the Group Company Secretary, in consultation with the Group Chief Executive Officer. ... once a Trade has been made by or for a Director or Senior Executive, details of the Trade ... must be notified by email to the Group Company Secretary within 2 business days of execution of the Trade.

clearance.approver: Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: once a Trade has been made by or for a Director or Senior Executive, details of the Trade, including the date, number and price of HMC Capital Group Securities involved, must be notified by email to the Group Company Secretary within 2 business days of execution of the Trade.

clearance.approver: Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: A Designated Staff Member must first check the Restricted List if it wishes to trade in any Third Party Securities. If the Third Party Security ... is on that list, that member must first make a prior written request for pre-approval to the Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Company Secretary

carve_outs: exercise of employee options or performance rights to acquire HMC Capital Group Securities at the specified exercise price
sale of HMC Capital Group Securities that have been converted after exercising options or rights
short_term.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling HMC Capital Group Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (e.g. forward contracts).

exceptions.evidence: an exercise (but not the sale of HMC Capital Group Securities following exercise) of an option or other right to acquire HMC Capital Group Securities under an employee incentive scheme or the conversion of a convertible HMC Capital Group Security, where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Blackout Period
Trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most securityholders in a listed Group Entity or LPT such as a rights or entitlement issue, a security purchase plan, or an equal access buy-back
Trading where the beneficial interest in the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities does not change.

an acquisition of HMC Capital Group Securities under a dividend/distribution reinvestment plan, provided the election to participate ... was not made during a Blackout Period or when the Employee was in possession of any inside information
an Employee accepting a takeover bid or transferring HMC Capital Group Securities under a scheme of arrangement in respect of a Group Entity or LPT

an involuntary disposal of HMC Capital Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
an acquisition of HMC Capital Group Securities under a bonus issue made on the same terms to all holders of HMC Capital Group Securities of the same class

where a Group Entity has an employee incentive scheme with an Employee as a trustee of the scheme, an acquisition of the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities by the Employee in their capacity as a trustee of the scheme

indirect and incidental Trading that occurs as a consequence of an Employee dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold HMC Capital Group Securities as part of its portfolio

where an Employee is a trustee of a trust, Trading by that trust provided the Employee is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to Trade during a Blackout Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the relevant Employee

exceptions.approver: Group Company Secretary and Group Chief Executive Officer (pre-clearance of the plan itself)
exceptions.evidence: Trading under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... where ... the trading plan does not permit the Employee to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or where to Trade

exceptions.approver: Group Company Secretary and Group CEO (Chair of the Company for the CEO's own proposed trading)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship, where the Employee has pressing financial commitments that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling HMC Capital Group Securities

exceptions.approver: Group Company Secretary and Group CEO (Chair of the Company for the CEO's own proposed trading)
exceptions.evidence: requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements.

financing_disclosure: Directors and Senior Executives: consent from the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary (or the Chair of the Company for the CEO's or Company Secretary's own margin lending) required before entering a margin lending arrangement, transferring securities into an existing margin loan account, or otherwise trading pursuant to such an arrangement.

exemption_authority: Permission to sell (not purchase) during a Blackout Period will ordinarily only be granted in Exceptional Circumstances (severe financial hardship, or court order/other legal or regulatory requirement) and only if the person is not in possession of inside information; approval is by the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary (or Chair of the Company for the CEO's or Company Secretary's own proposed trading), is entirely discretionary, confidential if refused, valid 5 trading days from grant unless otherwise specified, and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced-sale exception conditioned on prior consent
bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of HMC Capital Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale under a properly consented loan is excused from the Blackout Period ban; but if the loan itself was never cleared under section 8.1, the forced-sale exception is unavailable and the enforcement sale would breach the policy - so obtaining upfront consent for the loan is essential to preserve the bank's enforcement rights.

bespoke_clauses.topic: consent can be conditioned on margin-call sale terms
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Group Entity may, at its discretion, make any consent granted under section 8.1 conditional upon such terms and conditions that the relevant Group Entity sees fit (for example, specifying the circumstances in which HMC Capital Group Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement mechanics for a funded collar could be pre-negotiated and built into the consent itself, giving more structuring flexibility than a blanket-ban policy would allow.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Employee who holds HMC Capital Group Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to Trade in the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities during that time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Units under ASX escrow or a voluntary lock-up cannot be collared or pledged at all, regardless of vesting state, until the escrow period ends.

bespoke_clauses.topic: pre-approval required at all times, not just in closed periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: When permitted to Trade in accordance with this Policy, or where Trading is proposed during a Blackout Period, all Directors and Employees must give a prior written request for pre-approval to the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary of any proposed Trading
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike open-window-only policies, every leg of a collar (entry, unwind, or roll) needs individual case-by-case pre-approval regardless of the Blackout Period calendar, adding execution friction and a 5-trading-day validity window to each step.

summary: A funded collar is achievable for Directors and Senior Executives under this policy, but only once the HDN units are vested and free of any holding lock, dealing restriction or ASX/voluntary escrow, and only with layered consent. The put and call legs, expressly caught as 'Financial Products' operating to limit economic risk, are absolutely prohibited over unvested units or units still subject to a holding lock, with no waiver; once vested and unrestricted they require prior written pre-approval from the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary (Chair and Company Secretary for a Director), certifying no inside information, executed within 5 trading days of approval and generally outside the Blackout Periods (1 January to 1 business day after half-year results; 1 July to 1 business day after annual results). The loan leg is directly addressed: including the units in a margin loan portfolio, transferring them into a margin loan account, or otherwise trading under a margin lending arrangement all require the same CEO/Company Secretary (or Chair) consent, which may be made conditional on the circumstances in which units can be sold to satisfy a margin call, and a lender's forced sale during a Blackout Period is excused from breach only if that consent was obtained beforehand. Directors and Senior Executives must also notify the Company Secretary of every trade within 2 business days, and any dealing on behalf of an associate needs the same pre-approval. Overall, a funded collar can be implemented on vested, unrestricted, non-escrowed units once the requisite consents for both the derivatives and the secured financing are obtained in advance, with the bank's enforcement rights preserved only if the loan was cleared upfront.
